bill.title: United States Commission on International Religious Freedom Reauthorization Act of 2026
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 505.
subjects: U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom
bill.officialSummary: United States Commission on International Religious Freedom Reauthorization Act of 2026 This bill reauthorizes the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom through FY2028. The commission is an independent federal commission tasked with monitoring international religious freedom conditions, reviewing U.S. government policy, and making policy recommendations.

classification.plainSummary: This bill extends the authorization for the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom through fiscal year 2028. The commission is an independent federal body that monitors religious freedom conditions around the world, reviews U.S. government policies on the issue, and makes recommendations. The bill does not appear to change the commission's structure or mandate, only its funding authorization period.

plain.whatItDoes: This bill would renew the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom through the 2028 budget year.
plain.whoItTouches: Mostly people outside the United States. It reaches most readers here only indirectly.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in what the United States does abroad. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.
plain.source: Reworded from the official summary. Staff at the Congressional Research Service wrote that summary. It is public domain, and the full text of it is further down this page.
